title: Read-only intake of an existing repository
where: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Perform a comprehensive read-only audit of the repository {{REPO_PATH}} for project {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- README.md, package.json, pom.xml, go.mod, or Cargo.toml
- .env.example, docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile
- .github/workflows/ or CI configuration files

Constraints:
- Do not modify, create, or delete any source files or configuration files.
- Do not commit or push any changes.
- Do not print or extract any secrets, environment tokens, or sensitive credentials.

Context:
- One-line summary: {{ONE_LINE}}
- Target users: {{USERS}}
- Tech stack: {{STACK}}
- Timeframe: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Produce a markdown report summarizing:
1. Identified languages, package managers, and pinned runtime versions.
2. Commands required to install dependencies, run the test suite, and start local development.
3. Presence and coverage of existing automated tests.
4. Obvious security or dependency warnings.

Acceptance check:
Verify that git status is completely clean before finishing.

Report format:
Conclude your response by listing:
- What files you inspected
- What you verified
- What you could not verify without executing untrusted scripts
stop_when: The read-only audit report is generated and git status confirms zero modified files.

title: Map the repo and risks without changing it
where: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Map the architectural component boundaries and operational risk factors in {{REPO_PATH}} for {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- Top-level directory structure
- Entrypoint files (e.g., src/index.ts, src/main.tsx, server.ts, cmd/main.go)
- Configuration manifests and database migration directories

Constraints:
- Strictly read-only: do not edit, rename, or delete existing code.
- Do not introduce new dependencies.
- Keep risk analysis factual based solely on code evidence.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}} ({{ONE_LINE}})
- Primary stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Provide a structured risk assessment detailing:
1. Component Map: client surfaces, API services, database interactions, and third-party integrations.
2. Technical Debt Hotspots: oversized files (>500 lines), circular dependencies, and unmaintained packages.
3. Operational Risks: missing branch protection indicators, unpinned action hashes, or missing health check endpoints.
4. Immediate stabilization recommendations ranked by priority.

Acceptance check:
Run git status to verify zero file modifications.

Report format:
State what you reviewed, what tests or scripts were observed, and what runtime behaviors remain unverified.
stop_when: The architectural risk map is rendered with zero git modifications.

title: Bootstrap clean dev environment
where: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Validate and document a deterministic local development setup for {{PROJECT_NAME}} in {{REPO_PATH}}.

Files to read first:
- README.md
- .env.example
- package.json or build tool definitions
- Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml (if present)

Constraints:
- Do not alter business domain logic.
- Never write production credentials or private keys to .env files.
- Pin all installed tools to the versions specified in {{STACK}}.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Target delivery window: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
1. Verify or create docs/DEVELOPMENT.md with step-by-step setup commands.
2. Ensure single-command bootstrap starts the app on localhost.
3. Verify test runner succeeds from a clean checkout.

Acceptance check:
Run the test command and verify zero failures. Run git diff to ensure only documentation and template examples were touched.

Report format:
Report what files were updated, what verification commands were executed, and what manual dependencies require developer intervention.
stop_when: The development setup guide is documented and the local test suite passes cleanly.

title: Interview me before any build
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini Chat
text:
Goal: Challenge assumptions and interview the engineering team regarding {{PROJECT_NAME}} before writing any code.

Files to read first:
- docs/charter.md (if present)
- README.md

Constraints:
- Do not generate code, scaffolding, or boilerplate.
- Ask exactly one to three questions at a time; wait for responses before continuing.
- Do not make flattering remarks; focus on critical failure modes.

Context:
- Purpose: {{ONE_LINE}}
- Target users: {{USERS}}
- Tech stack: {{STACK}}
- Timeframe: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Conduct a rigorous discovery interview covering:
1. The specific friction event that forces {{USERS}} to seek an alternative.
2. Current manual workarounds (spreadsheets, scripts) and their quantified cost.
3. The single metric that defines success for {{TIMEFRAME}}.
4. The primary technical bottleneck that could derail delivery.

Acceptance check:
Summarize the confirmed answers into a draft problem statement with all unresolved assumptions flagged.

Report format:
Summarize confirmed facts, remaining blind spots, and what has not been verified.
stop_when: The user interview finishes and key user assumptions are cataloged.

title: Separate facts from assumptions
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Audit the concept and value proposition for {{PROJECT_NAME}} by separating verified evidence from unproven assumptions.

Files to read first:
- docs/research/ or docs/charter.md (if existing)
- README.md

Constraints:
- Read-only analysis: do not modify application code.
- Base facts only on user interview data, system logs, or documented analytics.
- Treat all developer hypotheses as assumptions until proven.

Context:
- App summary: {{ONE_LINE}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Target timeline: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Produce a two-column classification table in docs/research/assumptions.md:
1. Verified Facts (with cited user quotes, metrics, or API proofs).
2. Risky Assumptions (feasibility, willingness to adopt, workflow fit).
3. De-risking Spikes: for each high-risk assumption, write the smallest experiment to test it in under 48 hours.

Acceptance check:
Ensure each de-risking experiment has a binary pass/fail criterion.

Report format:
Report files created or reviewed, tests performed, and unverified assumptions.
stop_when: docs/research/assumptions.md is written with testable pass/fail criteria.

title: Harden the requirements
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Transform ambiguous feature desires for {{PROJECT_NAME}} into unambiguous, testable user stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md or docs/requirements/ (if present)
- README.md

Constraints:
- Do not write implementation code.
- Do not use vague terms like 'fast', 'intuitive', 'secure', or 'user-friendly'.
- Every acceptance scenario must be verifiable by automated tests.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Summary: {{ONE_LINE}}
- Target users: {{USERS}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Update or generate docs/PRD.md containing:
1. User persona profile for {{USERS}}.
2. Functional user stories with strict Given-When-Then scenarios (happy path, validation error, edge case).
3. Explicit Non-Functional Requirements (P95 latency under load, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, data retention).
4. Explicit Non-Goals for the initial release.

Acceptance check:
Confirm every story has at least 3 concrete Gherkin scenarios with deterministic verification criteria.

Report format:
Report the requirements updated, the validation checklist used, and what stakeholder approvals remain unverified.
stop_when: docs/PRD.md is written with Given-When-Then acceptance criteria for all MVP stories.

title: Define non-functional performance and accessibility limits
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Establish quantifiable Non-Functional Requirements (NFR) budgets for {{PROJECT_NAME}} on {{STACK}}.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (if present)

Constraints:
- Do not modify existing application code.
- Use industry standards: W3C WCAG 2.2 AA and Google Core Web Vitals.
- All targets must have a numeric threshold and designated measurement tool.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Architecture: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Create docs/requirements/nfr.md with:
1. Latency targets: P50 < 100ms, P95 < 300ms, P99 < 800ms for API endpoints.
2. Frontend Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms.
3. Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios (>= 4.5:1), keyboard operability, aria labels.
4. Scalability & Availability: Target uptime (99.9%), maximum concurrent active users.

Acceptance check:
Verify every row contains: Metric, Numeric Target, Measurement Tool, and Alert Trigger.

Report format:
List documentation changed, tools identified, and unverified load conditions.
stop_when: docs/requirements/nfr.md is committed with quantitative budgets for all four pillars.

title: Cut the scope to the core
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Apply ruthless MoSCoW prioritization to lock the MVP scope for {{PROJECT_NAME}} before Gate G1.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md
- docs/charter.md

Constraints:
- Do not add new feature ideas.
- Must-Have list must fit within delivery window: {{TIMEFRAME}}.
- Do not change existing code.

Context:
- Core value: {{ONE_LINE}}
- Target users: {{USERS}}
- Tech stack: {{STACK}}
- Timeframe: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Author docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md with:
1. Must-Have: The single critical path (max 3-5 user stories) required to validate {{ONE_LINE}}.
2. Should-Have: High-value features deferred to post-MVP Milestone 2.
3. Won't-Have: Explicit list of rejected features to protect scope.
4. Milestone checkpoints mapping to {{TIMEFRAME}} with weekly demo goals.

Acceptance check:
Verify the Must-Have critical path takes less than 3 minutes for {{USERS}} to complete.

Report format:
Report what scope was cut, the milestone schedule produced, and what team capacity assumptions remain unverified.
stop_when: docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md contains signed scope-lock boundary ready for Gate G1.

title: Milestone delivery slice definition
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Break the Must-Have MVP scope for {{PROJECT_NAME}} into thin, vertical, testable slices.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md
- docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md

Constraints:
- Slices must be end-to-end vertical (UI + API + DB), not horizontal technical layers.
- Each slice must be deliverable in under 1 week within {{TIMEFRAME}}.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Timeframe: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Document the milestone delivery slices in docs/milestones.md:
1. Slice 1: Walking Skeleton (deployable pipeline, database connected, ping endpoint).
2. Slice 2: Core Domain Action (happy path data creation and validation).
3. Slice 3: Core Retrieval & Feedback (user view, error states, and responsive UI).
4. Demonstration criteria and acceptance tests for each slice.

Acceptance check:
Verify every slice has an independent demo script and automated test validation.

Report format:
State documentation created, sequencing logic, and unverified velocity estimates.
stop_when: docs/milestones.md defines thin vertical slices mapping to {{TIMEFRAME}}.

title: Skeptical architecture review
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Review proposed system architecture for {{PROJECT_NAME}} skeptically, identifying single points of failure and premature complexity.

Files to read first:
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md or docs/PRD.md
- docker-compose.yml or infra/ definitions (if present)

Constraints:
- Challenge unnecessary microservices, esoteric message queues, or premature caching.
- Do not add third-party cloud services unless required by {{ONE_LINE}}.
- Favor standard boring technology matching {{STACK}}.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Produce docs/architecture/review.md detailing:
1. Architectural Critique: unnecessary hops, network boundaries, or distributed transactions.
2. Single Points of Failure (SPOF) and catastrophic failure scenarios.
3. Latency & Network Budget: estimated round-trip times across component boundaries.
4. Recommended simplification plan preserving high reliability.

Acceptance check:
Verify that the simplified architecture can run locally with a single docker-compose or start command.

Report format:
Report components critiqued, simplifications proposed, and unverified throughput limits.
stop_when: docs/architecture/review.md provides a defensible, simplified component topology.

title: Write an ADR for one decision
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Author a formal Architecture Decision Record (ADR) for a key technical trade-off in {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- docs/adr/ (inspect existing ADR numbering)
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- package.json

Constraints:
- Follow the Michael Nygard ADR format (Context, Options, Decision, Consequences).
- Evaluate at least 3 concrete alternatives; do not write a biased justification.
- Do not commit secrets or provider credentials.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Tech stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Create docs/adr/NNNN-decision-title.md:
1. Context: Problem statement and architectural constraints driving the decision.
2. Options Considered: Pros and cons for three distinct architectural approaches.
3. Decision: Chosen option and explicit justification.
4. Consequences: Positive gains, accepted technical debt, and mitigation strategies.

Acceptance check:
Verify the ADR file uses the next sequential index and markdown headings match ADR convention.

Report format:
State the ADR filename created, alternatives weighed, and unverified vendor roadmaps.
stop_when: The ADR is written and saved to docs/adr/ with status Accepted.

title: Schema review
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Review database schema for {{PROJECT_NAME}} for referential integrity, indexing strategy, and migration safety.

Files to read first:
- Schema files (e.g., prisma/schema.prisma, src/db/schema.ts, migrations/, init.sql)
- docs/PRD.md

Constraints:
- All foreign keys must have corresponding indexes on child tables.
- Primary keys must be typed consistently (UUIDv7 or BigInt).
- Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) must be UTC.
- Do not run destructive DROP queries.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Purpose: {{ONE_LINE}}

Required output:
Provide docs/db/schema-audit.md with:
1. Entity relationship and normalization critique.
2. Missing indexes for high-frequency filters, joins, and sorting.
3. Nullability rules and foreign key ON DELETE policies (CASCADE vs RESTRICT).
4. Zero-downtime migration review: flag any operations that lock tables in production.

Acceptance check:
Verify that all migration DDL scripts can execute UP and DOWN without data corruption.

Report format:
List schema files inspected, query bottlenecks identified, and unverified query plan benchmarks.
stop_when: docs/db/schema-audit.md is authored with verified indexing and constraint safety.

title: Draft zero-downtime migration step
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Write an expand-and-contract migration script for modifying a database table in {{PROJECT_NAME}} without application downtime.

Files to read first:
- Current database schema definition
- Latest database migration scripts

Constraints:
- Never drop or rename columns in the same release as the application code change.
- Follow the 4-phase expand/backfill/switch/contract pattern.
- Do not lock high-traffic tables with default value rewrites.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Database: PostgreSQL / relational database

Required output:
Create migration scripts in the repository migration directory:
1. Phase 1 (Expand): Add nullable new column or dual-write trigger.
2. Phase 2 (Backfill): Batched background script backfilling existing rows without table locks.
3. Rollback script reversing the step cleanly.

Acceptance check:
Execute the migration runner in test environment; assert both UP and DOWN migrations succeed.

Report format:
Report migration files created, execution status in local database, and unverified production table sizes.
stop_when: Expand-and-contract migration script and rollback file pass test database run.

title: Contract first
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Draft an OpenAPI 3.1 specification for {{PROJECT_NAME}} before implementing backend routes.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md
- Existing route handlers (if any in {{REPO_PATH}})

Constraints:
- Adhere to RESTful conventions: plural nouns, HTTP verbs, standard status codes.
- Define error payloads using RFC 9457 Problem Details (application/problem+json).
- Do not invent custom non-standard error structures.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}} ({{ONE_LINE}})
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Tech stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Create or update docs/api/openapi.yaml containing:
1. Complete endpoint definitions for all MVP user stories.
2. Request bodies with field-level type and validation constraints.
3. Standard 2xx, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, and 500 responses.
4. RFC 9457 Problem Details schema component.

Acceptance check:
Run OpenAPI linter (e.g., npx @stoplight/spectral-cli lint docs/api/openapi.yaml) with zero errors.

Report format:
Report schema files modified, linter output, and unverified client SDK generation.
stop_when: docs/api/openapi.yaml passes Spectral linter with zero errors.

title: RFC 9457 error handler implementation
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Implement an RFC 9457 Problem Details error handler middleware for {{PROJECT_NAME}} in {{STACK}}.

Files to read first:
- docs/api/openapi.yaml
- Server entrypoint and route middleware setup

Constraints:
- Response Content-Type must be 'application/problem+json'.
- Must include: type, title, status, detail, instance.
- Never leak internal database stack traces, SQL syntax errors, or server secrets to client responses in production.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Repository: {{REPO_PATH}}

Required output:
1. TypeScript error classes mapping domain errors to HTTP status codes.
2. Centralized error handling middleware formatting all thrown errors into RFC 9457.
3. Unit tests asserting RFC 9457 payload format for 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, and 500 Internal Error.

Acceptance check:
Run test suite verifying error responses contain exact RFC 9457 fields and sanitized 500 error IDs.

Report format:
Report middleware files created, tests executed, and unverified edge proxies.
stop_when: Error handling middleware and unit tests verifying RFC 9457 compliance pass.

title: Build one slice, test first
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Build a single interactive user interface slice for {{PROJECT_NAME}} following test-first principles.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md (relevant user story)
- src/components/ or design tokens
- Existing UI tests

Constraints:
- Write component tests before or alongside UI code.
- Use semantic HTML (<main>, <nav>, <button>, <label>); no clickable div wrappers.
- Support responsive viewport down to 390px with zero horizontal scroll.
- Do not change unrelated components.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Component test asserting user interaction, state transition, and keyboard navigation.
2. Accessible React/TypeScript component implementing the slice.
3. Loading and error states.

Acceptance check:
Run component test suite (npm test or vitest); assert 100% passing tests with visible focus rings.

Report format:
State components created, tests passing, and unverified visual styling at other viewports.
stop_when: Component tests pass and component renders cleanly without horizontal scroll.

title: Accessibility audit of one page
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Conduct an accessibility audit of a key page in {{PROJECT_NAME}} against W3C WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

Files to read first:
- Page component and layout files
- Global stylesheet and theme tokens

Constraints:
- Compliance standard: WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Contrast ratio must be >= 4.5:1 for normal text, >= 3:1 for large text.
- Every interactive element must have a visible focus outline and accessible name.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Audit checklist of the target page covering landmark roles, keyboard navigation, and form labels.
2. Fixes for missing htmlFor/id label bindings, missing aria-expanded attributes, and low contrast.
3. Automated accessibility test using axe-core or Playwright.

Acceptance check:
Run automated axe accessibility check; assert zero critical or serious accessibility violations.

Report format:
Report accessibility bugs resolved, tests run, and unverified screen reader combinations.
stop_when: Automated axe-core accessibility checks pass with zero violations.

title: Implement one business rule
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Implement a core domain business rule in {{PROJECT_NAME}} with tests first and boundary validation.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md (business requirements)
- Domain service files in {{REPO_PATH}}

Constraints:
- Decouple pure domain business logic from HTTP frameworks and database clients.
- Validate all inputs strictly at the perimeter before executing domain rules.
- Do not alter unrelated business services.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Core purpose: {{ONE_LINE}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Pure unit tests asserting calculation math, state transitions, and edge cases.
2. Domain service module implementing the business rule.
3. Input validation schema enforcing boundary invariants.

Acceptance check:
Run unit tests; assert 100% pass rate in under 1 second with boundary edge cases covered.

Report format:
Report domain modules created, test assertions verified, and unverified database integrations.
stop_when: Domain service and unit tests pass with all edge cases verified.

title: Perimeter validation and transaction wrapper
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Implement request validation and database transaction safety for a mutating endpoint in {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- docs/api/openapi.yaml
- Controller and database repository files

Constraints:
- Never trust client inputs; validate body, query params, and headers.
- Wrap multi-table operations in ACID transaction blocks with automatic rollback.
- No raw unsanitized SQL queries.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}

Required output:
1. Validation schema (Zod/TypeBox/Joi) matching the OpenAPI contract.
2. Route controller with validation middleware.
3. Transaction wrapper ensuring atomicity during multi-table writes.
4. Integration test asserting rollback on failure.

Acceptance check:
Run integration test asserting that simulated mid-transaction failure leaves zero orphan records.

Report format:
List controllers updated, transaction tests executed, and unverified connection pool limits.
stop_when: Transaction rollback integration tests pass cleanly.

title: STRIDE threat model
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Conduct a STRIDE threat model analysis for the core architecture of {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/api/openapi.yaml
- Authentication and authorization middleware

Constraints:
- Base threats on actual architecture in {{STACK}}, not generic boilerplate.
- Do not store or print real security tokens or secrets.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Architecture: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Create docs/security/stride-threat-model.md analyzing:
1. Spoofing: Authentication bypass and token replay vectors.
2. Tampering: Parameter tampering, SQL injection, and XSS risks.
3. Repudiation: Audit log completeness for sensitive operations.
4. Information Disclosure: PII leakage, stack trace leaks, and insecure headers.
5. Denial of Service: Unbounded payload limits, slow queries, and missing rate limits.
6. Elevation of Privilege: BOLA/IDOR and role escalation paths.
For every threat, provide concrete code-level mitigations.

Acceptance check:
Verify every identified threat has an assigned mitigation owner and testable check.

Report format:
Report threats cataloged, mitigations reviewed, and unverified third-party dependencies.
stop_when: docs/security/stride-threat-model.md is documented with mitigations for each STRIDE category.

title: Attacker-minded diff review
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Review recent code changes in {{REPO_PATH}} from the perspective of an attacker targeting OWASP ASVS and API Top 10.

Files to read first:
- git diff against main branch (or target PR diff)
- docs/security/ or auth middleware

Constraints:
- Review diff skeptically looking for security flaws.
- Inspect for IDOR (can User A access User B's resource?), SSRF, SQLi, and secret leaks.
- Do not modify code during review.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Produce a security review comment detailing:
1. Authentication & Authorization audit of new endpoints.
2. Input sanitization and boundary checks.
3. Security header compliance (CSP, CORS, HSTS).
4. Secret scan: verify no tokens or keys are present in diff.

Acceptance check:
Run automated secret scanner (e.g. gitleaks or trufflehog) on the diff; verify zero findings.

Report format:
Report diff commits inspected, security findings ranked by CVSS, and unverified network configurations.
stop_when: Security audit report is produced and secret scanner passes with zero findings.

title: Behaviour tests from acceptance criteria
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Translate Given-When-Then acceptance criteria from docs/PRD.md into automated behavior tests for {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- docs/PRD.md
- Existing test files in tests/ or src/

Constraints:
- Test behavior and observable outcomes, not private internal methods.
- Tests must be deterministic and run in under 3 seconds.
- Do not mock the system under test; mock only external third parties.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Test specification file directly reflecting PRD Gherkin scenarios.
2. Happy path assertions.
3. Negative edge case assertions (invalid formats, missing auth, boundary values).

Acceptance check:
Run the test runner command; assert all newly created behavior tests pass with zero failures.

Report format:
Report test files created, scenarios covered, and unverified asynchronous timings.
stop_when: All behavior tests matching PRD acceptance criteria pass cleanly.

title: Automate integration test container
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Configure isolated integration tests using Testcontainers or Docker Compose for {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- docker-compose.yml
- Database connection and migration scripts
- Existing integration tests

Constraints:
- Tests must run against a real database instance (e.g., PostgreSQL), not SQLite mocks.
- Each test suite must start with fresh tables or isolated transactions.
- Do not connect to remote production databases.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Repository: {{REPO_PATH}}

Required output:
1. Integration test runner launching a containerized test database.
2. Automated schema migration execution before tests run.
3. CRUD integration test verifying actual database transactions.
4. Clean container teardown after tests complete.

Acceptance check:
Run integration test command; assert container boots, migrations run, tests pass, and container terminates.

Report format:
Report test scripts created, execution duration, and unverified cloud networking.
stop_when: Containerized integration tests execute migrations and pass cleanly.

title: Skeptical diff review
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Review a pull request diff in {{REPO_PATH}} with a skeptical staff-engineer mindset.

Files to read first:
- git diff against main
- .github/pull_request_template.md (if present)

Constraints:
- Enforce Conventional Commits specification.
- Reject PRs over 400 lines of code without architectural justification.
- Check for unhandled promises, memory leaks, and N+1 query patterns.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Produce a structured PR review:
1. Summary of changes and intent.
2. Correctness & Architecture: Logic bugs, concurrency risks, and invariant violations.
3. Testing Depth: Are edge cases and failure paths tested?
4. Performance & Resource Safety: Query complexity and unneeded re-renders.
5. Specific inline diff recommendations for any flagged issue.

Acceptance check:
Verify that all suggested improvements include concrete code snippet replacements.

Report format:
State commits reviewed, issues categorized by severity (High/Med/Low), and unverified runtime telemetry.
stop_when: Diff review is generated with actionable line-by-line feedback.

title: PR size and complexity audit
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Audit open pull requests and branches in {{REPO_PATH}} for size, cyclomatic complexity, and test ratio.

Files to read first:
- git log, git status, and PR diff
- Code quality configuration (.eslintrc, biome.json, or tsconfig.json)

Constraints:
- Do not modify application code.
- Provide concrete recommendations to break oversized branches into smaller atomic PRs.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Delivery timeframe: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Provide a branch audit report in docs/reviews/pr-audit.md:
1. Total line additions and deletions.
2. Test-to-code ratio (aim for >= 1:1 on new domain logic).
3. Step-by-step cherry-pick or decomposition plan if PR exceeds 400 lines.

Acceptance check:
Verify the decomposition plan allows each sub-PR to build and pass tests independently.

Report format:
Report branches evaluated, proposed PR splits, and unverified merge conflict states.
stop_when: docs/reviews/pr-audit.md outlines atomic PR breakdown passing independent tests.

title: Find the bottleneck
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Measure and isolate the primary performance bottleneck in {{PROJECT_NAME}} before Gate G3.

Files to read first:
- High-traffic API route handlers and database queries
- Frontend client bundles and entrypoints
- docs/requirements/nfr.md

Constraints:
- Measure first: never apply speculative optimizations without baseline profiling data.
- Test under realistic data volume, not empty tables.
- Do not change functional behavior.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Target P95 latency: < 300ms

Required output:
Generate docs/performance/bottleneck-audit.md detailing:
1. Measured baseline latency or bundle metrics (P50, P95, P99).
2. Root cause analysis: CPU bound, memory bound, N+1 query, or bundle weight.
3. Surgical optimization patch.
4. Post-optimization benchmark proving measurable gain.

Acceptance check:
Run benchmark command verifying that P95 latency or bundle weight improved by at least 20%.

Report format:
Report benchmarks run, optimizations applied, and unverified production CDN conditions.
stop_when: docs/performance/bottleneck-audit.md demonstrates measured improvement against baseline.

title: Frontend Web Vitals and bundle audit
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Audit and optimize client bundle footprint and Core Web Vitals for {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- Bundler configuration (vite.config.ts, next.config.js)
- Main client entrypoints and routing tables
- package.json dependencies

Constraints:
- Keep initial gzipped JavaScript bundle under 150KB.
- Meet Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms.
- Do not sacrifice accessibility for bundle size.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Bundle visualizer report analyzing heaviest dependency chunks.
2. Implementation of dynamic route splitting and lazy loading for heavy modals.
3. Core Web Vitals verification report.

Acceptance check:
Run build command (e.g. npm run build); inspect dist/ chunk sizes and assert main chunk is within budget.

Report format:
Report chunks analyzed, code-splitting applied, and unverified low-end mobile hardware.
stop_when: Production build succeeds with all bundle chunks within defined size budgets.

title: Pipeline review
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Audit CI/CD workflows for {{PROJECT_NAME}} against security best practices and speed benchmarks.

Files to read first:
- .github/workflows/*.yml or CI definitions
- Dockerfile
- package.json scripts

Constraints:
- Enforce least-privilege permissions (e.g. permissions: contents: read).
- Pin all GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs, not mutable tags.
- Cache dependency layers to keep total pipeline time under 5 minutes.
- Never echo secrets or tokens into CI logs.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Updated CI workflow file with:
1. Parallelized lint, unit test, and security scan jobs.
2. Dependency caching keys.
3. Container build with non-root security context.
4. OIDC integration replacing static long-lived credentials.

Acceptance check:
Validate workflow syntax using actionlint or schema validator; assert zero syntax or security warnings.

Report format:
Report workflow files updated, security hardenings applied, and unverified cloud deployment runners.
stop_when: CI workflow passes actionlint with pinned actions and least-privilege tokens.

title: Ephemeral PR environment configuration
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Configure automated preview environments for every pull request in {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:

- Dockerfile and deployment scripts

Constraints:
- Previews must be ephemeral: spin up on PR open and tear down on PR close/merge.
- Preview URLs must be isolated from production databases.
- Do not leak staging or prod secrets.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. CI workflow job building preview container on PR events.
2. Deployment step outputting unique preview URL to pull request comments.
3. Teardown workflow triggered on pull request closure.

Acceptance check:
Validate workflow logic; verify preview URL generation and cleanup event triggers.

Report format:
Report workflow files created, cleanup mechanisms configured, and unverified DNS wildcards.
stop_when: PR preview and cleanup workflows are defined and validated.

title: Release plan
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Author an operational release and rollback plan for {{PROJECT_NAME}} prior to Gate G4.

Files to read first:

- docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md
- Infrastructure and deployment configurations

Constraints:
- Plan must include concrete rollback triggers and automated health checks.
- Zero-downtime: migrations and deployments must support rolling updates.
- Do not write secrets or tokens into the runbook.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Release window: {{TIMEFRAME}}

Required output:
Create docs/releases/release-plan.md detailing:
1. Pre-flight verification checklist.
2. Expand/backfill/switch/contract migration sequence.
3. Canary or rolling deployment progression (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
4. Explicit rollback criteria (e.g. 5xx rate > 1% over 2 minutes) and exact rollback CLI command.

Acceptance check:
Verify every deployment step has an explicit verification command and rollback counterpart.

Report format:
Report runbooks created, verification commands listed, and unverified DNS propagation latency.
stop_when: docs/releases/release-plan.md contains verified deployment and rollback commands for Gate G4.

title: Health check probes and rollback dry-run
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Implement HTTP liveness (/healthz) and readiness (/readyz) probes and simulate a deployment rollback in {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Files to read first:
- Server routing and initialization files
- Database connection pool configuration

Constraints:
- /healthz must check process liveness with minimal overhead (< 5ms).
- /readyz must verify database connection pool and cache readiness.
- Probes must never leak credentials or internal stack details.

Context:
- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}

Required output:
1. /healthz endpoint returning HTTP 200 when service is running.
2. /readyz endpoint returning 200 when database ping succeeds and 503 during warm-up.
3. Integration test asserting both probe responses.

Acceptance check:
Run test suite verifying /readyz returns 503 when database is disconnected and 200 when ready.

Report format:
Report probe controllers created, tests executed, and unverified load balancer health intervals.
stop_when: Health and readiness probe tests pass with proper status code handling.

title: Alert audit
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Audit monitoring alerts for {{PROJECT_NAME}} to eliminate alert fatigue and ensure high signal-to-noise.

Files to read first:
- Monitoring and alerting rules (e.g., prometheus.yml, terraform/alerts, datadog/)
- docs/requirements/nfr.md

Constraints:
- Alert on symptoms affecting {{USERS}} (high error rate, elevated latency), not background noise (CPU blips).
- Every alert must have an assigned severity (SEV-1 vs SEV-2) and link to an actionable runbook.
- If an alert requires no human action, delete or silence it.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Tech stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
Generate docs/monitoring/alert-audit.md with:
1. SLO definitions: Availability (99.9%) and Latency (P95 < 300ms).
2. Critical Alert Rules: Four Golden Signals (Latency, Traffic, Errors, Saturation).
3. Alert catalog mapping every alert to its root runbook documentation.
4. Notification routing schedule (PagerDuty/Slack/Email).

Acceptance check:
Verify every alert rule specifies: Threshold, Duration, Severity, and Runbook URL.

Report format:
List alert configurations audited, noisy rules eliminated, and unverified paging integrations.
stop_when: docs/monitoring/alert-audit.md maps every critical alert to an actionable runbook.

title: Instrument Golden Signals telemetry
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Instrument OpenTelemetry or Prometheus metrics for the Four Golden Signals in {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}

3. /metrics endpoint (or OTLP exporter) publishing telemetry.
4. Unit test asserting metric increments on simulated requests.

Run test suite asserting telemetry middleware records request duration and status without throwing.

Report format:
Report telemetry files added, metrics verified, and unverified remote collector endpoints.
stop_when: Telemetry middleware and metric unit tests pass successfully.

title: Monthly health report

text:

Generate docs/maintenance/monthly-health-report.md covering:

title: Disaster recovery drill runbook

text:

- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Audience: {{USERS}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Author docs/runbooks/disaster-recovery.md detailing:

Report runbooks created, command syntaxes verified, and unverified cloud snapshot drill runs.

title: Refactor component for zero layout shift
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:

- Stack: {{STACK}}
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}

Run automated Lighthouse or Web Vitals audit; assert CLS score < 0.05 on mobile viewport.

Report format:
Report component files refactored, skeleton loaders introduced, and unverified custom font CDNs.
stop_when: Component renders with CLS < 0.05 and passes component tests.

title: Idempotency key enforcement on mutating endpoints
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Implement Idempotency-Key header support for financial and mutating endpoints in {{PROJECT_NAME}}.

Constraints:
- Honor Idempotency-Key header on POST and PATCH requests.
- Store in-flight and completed responses in Redis with 24-hour expiration.
- Never execute duplicate transactions for identical idempotency keys.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Idempotency middleware checking Redis for existing key lock and cached payload.
2. Integration tests asserting replay of exact cached response without re-executing domain service.
3. Error response (409 Conflict) if a request with identical key is currently in-flight.

Acceptance check:
Run integration test sending concurrent identical idempotency keys; verify exactly one mutation executes.

Report format:
Report middleware files created, test scenarios executed, and unverified Redis multi-region replication.
stop_when: Idempotency middleware and concurrent replay integration tests pass cleanly.

title: Content-Security-Policy and security headers implementation
where: Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI
text:
Goal: Configure strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) and HTTP security headers for {{PROJECT_NAME}} on {{STACK}}.

Context:
- Project: {{PROJECT_NAME}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}

Required output:
1. Security header middleware configured for production environment.
2. Integration tests asserting header presence on all HTTP responses.
3. Documentation in docs/security/headers.md explaining policy directives.

Run integration test asserting presence of CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy headers.

Report format:
Report middleware files modified, test assertions verified, and unverified external script tags.
stop_when: Security headers middleware is active and automated header tests pass.
